incident-bot: PAGER: KV cache growth alert for route /v1/generate — 95th p99 token mem spike, autoscaler throttling. Pager level: P1. Paging oncall: @maya.

maya: On it. Any initial customer impact?

cust-success-bot: Two customers reported elevated latencies and some 429s in the last 10m (acct: seed-ai, acct: lumenhealth). They see timeouts on long-context calls.

jon: Looks like continuous batching + speculative decoding is producing many divergent drafts, which are getting inserted into KV cache. Cache keys exploded. Logs: `kvcache.insert_rate 120k/min` normal is ~3k/min.

alex: Copy. Pasted snippet from runtime logs: ```
[kv-cache] insert key=ctx:abc123:offset=0 len=2048 mode=speculative ts=1769001101
[kv-cache] insert key=ctx:abc123:offset=0 len=2048 mode=speculative ts=1769001102
[kv-cache] evicted key=ctx:abc123:offset=0 reason=dup_variant ts=1769001103
[kv-runtime] batch_size_mean=36 batch_tokens=4800 active_gpus=12
```

maya: That `mode=speculative` line is the smoking gun. Speculative decoding is creating variants and we're caching them before target commit, so later requests see many KV variants and continuous batching tries to combine them => combinatorial growth.

eva: Customer impact: increased latency and memory pressure triggered node-level OOMs intermittently, autoscaler cycled nodes -> request retries -> more speculative attempts -> feedback loop.

maya: Immediate mitigation plan (5m): 1) disable speculative decoding for the affected route(s) 2) reduce continuous batching window to 10ms 3) trigger kvcache TTL/flush for the hot keyspace.

jon: I can flip speculative decoding flag via runtime config. Command: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/configs/route -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","speculative_decoding":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED"`

deploy-bot: Starting config rollout for route /v1/generate (canary 5% -> 100%). Change: `speculative_decoding=false`. Trace: deploy-3182.

alex: Also proposing a short-term hotfix to avoid caching speculative entries: patch kvcache to reject inserts where mode=speculative. I can push a lightweight flag `kvcache.reject_speculative=true` to runtime without binary deploy.

maya: Do it. Jon, coordinate with Alex for the config gating. Keep canary small and watch insert_rate.

jon: Patching `kvcache.reject_speculative=true` now. `kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/runtime-kv KVCACHE_REJECT_SPECULATIVE=true`

[~2m later]

alex: Metrics update: insert_rate fell from 120k/min -> 8k/min in canary region. Memory pressure easing.

deploy-bot: Canary checked: no increased error rates at 5%. Rolling to 100%.

maya: Next reduce continuous batching window. Where's the config?

jon: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/configs/global -d '{"continuous_batching_ms":10}'` Applying.

deploy-bot: Continuous batching window update applied. Policy: aggressive low-latency.

eva: Observability note: we saw p95 latency drop from 1.6s -> 700ms after both mitigations. No further OOM events. Customers reporting reduced errors.

cust-success-bot: LumenHealth says their traffic is back to normal. Seed-ai confirms retries gone. They ask for root cause timeline.

maya: Good. We still need a long-term fix: ensure speculative drafts are not persisted to stable KV or have a separate ephemeral cache with strict TTL + no indexing. Also avoid continuous batching mixing divergent KV keys.

jon: Agree. Long-term action items: - Add draft/target sync check before kvcache insert (only insert when token confirmed) - Separate speculative cache pathway with lower capacity + GC - Add a model-serving policy to limit combinatorial draft branching per request

alex: Quick follow-up: we need a small patch to spec-decode module so that speculative variants carry a `transient` tag and kvcache only accepts non-transient. I'll draft PR after handoff.

maya: Oncall handoff: I need to go offline in 25m. @lee you'll take night oncall. Lee, current state: mitigations applied, insert rates down, batching window lowered, `kvcache.reject_speculative=true` set cluster-wide, canary rolled. Watch list: `kvcache.insert_rate`, `node_mem_available`, `p95_latency`, `error_429_rate`. Investigate any rollout regressions.

lee: Got it. I'll watch dashboards and set an alert if insert_rate spikes >20k/min or node_mem < 10% for >2min. Any quick runbook?

maya: Runbook snippets: ```
# Check insert rate
kubectl port-forward svc/metrics 9090:9090 && curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep kvcache_insert_rate
# Flush hot keyspace (if needed):
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/kvcache/flush" -d '{"prefix":"ctx:"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED"
# Toggle speculative back on (only after PR):
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/configs/route -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","speculative_decoding":true}'
```

lee: Thanks. I'll also disable further automatic node scale-ups for the next hour to avoid churn while we monitor.

deploy-bot: Note: A small rollback of `continuous_batching_ms` available via job rollback-642 if needed.

jon: Post-incident customer note: I recommend we proactively notify customers with affected accounts and include mitigation steps + ETA for long-term fixes.

cust-success-bot: I'll prepare a template and start outreach to Seed-AI and LumenHealth with current status and follow-up promises.

maya: Assigning follow-ups: 1) alex - PR for transient tag + kvcache gating (due EOD) 2) jon - design for speculative separate cache + GC policy (due 48h) 3) eng-runtime - propose batching policy changes to avoid mixing speculative variants (due 72h) 4) product/security - review for any data leakage from speculative drafts (due 72h).

alex: Acknowledged, will open PR and include unit tests for insert gating.

jon: I'll start an architecture doc for the separate cache and perf sims.

maya: Marking incident as mitigated at 1769004827. We'll run postmortem tomorrow. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

lee: Taking handoff. I'll ping if anything looks off.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated severity=P1 -> monitoring. Postmortem scheduled.

maya: Thanks team.
